thesis.problem: Restaurants still order from their suppliers by voicemail, fax and scribbled note, and a wholesaler's sales desk spends its morning transcribing those messages into an order system. Every transcription is a chance to send the wrong quantity, and the wrong quantity is food that gets thrown away.
thesis.solution: Choco gives the restaurant a messaging app for placing orders and the supplier a system that reads those orders straight into its own order processing, so the same instruction is only entered once. Selling to both sides of the same transaction is the point: the value only appears when the buyer and the seller are on the platform together.

sources.title: Choco chalks up $111 million, punches ticket at the unicorn club
sources.quote: Berlin-based food supply chain management platform Choco has raised $111 million in a Series B2 funding round at a valuation of $1.2 billion.

sources.title: Choco bites into $100M Series B, at a $600M valuation, to build a more transparent, sustainable food supply chain
sources.quote: Berlin-based Choco, which has built ordering software for restaurants and their suppliers, is working to digitize the food supply chain and announced $100 million in Series B funding, led by Left Lane Capital, to give it a $600 million post-market valuation.

sources.title: Choco Achieves Unicorn Status in Quest to Drive Zero Food Waste in Supply Chains
sources.quote: Choco, the technology company building a better food system for restaurants and suppliers, announced today that it has raised $111 million in Series B2 funding with a valuation of $1.2 billion.
